Dr David Smith
Cardiologist
Emergency Department
Main Hospital
Coast City

Dear Dr Smith,

Re: Mrs Lucy Clarke                               DOB: 11/03/1951

I am writing to refer Mrs Clarke who has a clinical picture consistent with unstable angina. Your
urgent assessment for admission and further management are highly appreciated.

On today’s review, Mrs Clarke presented with a one-week history of central crushing chest pain
radiating to the left arm which increased with exertion and relieved by rest. The duration of each
episode did not exceed 15 minutes. The pain was not associated with orthopnea, paroxysmal             Commented [OET1]: orthopnoea: you are using British
nocturnal dyspnea or palpitations. Her symptoms were associated with anxiety as she believed that     style of writing so please be consistent in your spelling
she had a heart attack. Her examination and her electrocardiograph were unremarkable.                 Commented [OET2]: dyspnoea

With regards to her risk factors for ischemic heart disease, Mrs Clarke is known to have diabetes
mellites, hyperlipidemia and hypertension. Additionally, her mother had a myocardial infarction       Commented [OET3]: hyperlipidaemia
and died of ischemic stroke. She is a non-smoker.

Mrs Clarke’s medications include sitagliptin 100 mg once a day, 25 units of NovoMix30 twice a day,
atorvastatin 40 mg once a day and irbesartan 75 mg once a day.

Mrs Clarke was counseled and advised about the risk of myocardial infarction. I would appreciate it   Commented [OET4]: counselled
if you could admit and manage her urgently. Should you require any help, do not hesitate to           Commented [OET5]: on
contact me.

Yours Sincerely
Doctor
